request:
Implement Session Refresh Rotation (CU-AUTH-03 / HU-03) at POST /api/identity/auth/refresh. Load and apply `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` and follow constitution rules:
1. Domain (`internal/domain`, stdlib only): ensure `ErrInvalidToken` is used for malformed, expired, or revoked refresh tokens.
2. Security Adapter (`internal/adapter/security/jwt_provider.go`): implement `Verify` using `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` restricted with `jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"})`, validating signature and `exp`, and returning `domain.ErrInvalidToken` on any failure.
3. Database (`db/queries/refresh_tokens.sql` + `sqlc generate`): add queries to fetch a refresh token record by `jti`, revoke a single token, revoke all active refresh tokens for a `user_id`, and insert a rotated refresh token. Keep compatibility with the existing `refresh_tokens` migration schema.
4. SQLite Adapter (`internal/adapter/sqlite/refresh_token_store.go`): implement atomic refresh rotation inside `*sql.Tx`â€”when an active, unexpired token is presented, revoke it and insert the new 7-day token; when an already-revoked token is reused (CA2), revoke all refresh tokens for that `user_id` and return `domain.ErrInvalidToken`.
5. Use Case (`internal/usecase/refresh_token.go`): implement `RefreshTokenUseCase.Execute(ctx, RefreshCommand{RefreshToken}) (AuthResult, error)` verifying the incoming token, loading the user (`UserRepository`), rotating the refresh token, and issuing a new 15-minute `accessToken` (`sub` and `role` claims) + new 7-day `refreshToken`.
6. HTTP, OpenAPI & Wiring: expose `POST /api/identity/auth/refresh` accepting `{"refreshToken": "..."}` and returning `200 OK` with `{"accessToken": "...", "refreshToken": "..."}`; apply `github.com/go-chi/httprate` rate limiting (10 attempts/min/IP -> `429`); map `domain.ErrInvalidToken` -> `401` (`INVALID_TOKEN`) in `respondError`; update `contracts/identity.openapi.yaml` and `shared/contracts/identity.openapi.yaml`; wire `RefreshTokenUseCase` in `cmd/api/main.go`.
7. Tests (stdlib `testing`): add unit tests for `RefreshTokenUseCase` (valid rotation, expired token, revoked token reuse revoking the entire user token chain), `:memory:` SQLite integration tests for atomic rotation and chain revocation, and `httptest` handler tests covering `200`, `400`, `401`, and `429`.
context: constraint: constitution mandates jwt/v5 with pinned HS256 and httprate for rate limits

FR-001.title: Refresh returns a new 15m access token and 7d refresh token

FR-002.title: The presented refresh token is revoked on use

FR-003.title: Malformed, expired, and unknown tokens return 401 INVALID_TOKEN

FR-004.title: Replaying a revoked token revokes the whole chain for that user

FR-005.title: Rotation is atomic: revoke and insert together or not at all

FR-006.title: Refresh attempts are limited to 10 per minute per IP

intent: Add POST /api/identity/auth/refresh with atomic rotation, reuse detection that revokes the whole chain, and a per-IP rate limit.

decisions.decision: Revoked refresh rows are kept with revoked_at set, never deleted.
decisions.why: Reuse detection needs to tell a spent token from a never-issued one; deleting erases the signal.

decisions.decision: The transaction lives in one repository method, Rotate, over *sql.Tx.
decisions.why: The adapter owns persistence; the use case should not orchestrate a transaction across calls.
decisions.rejected: A TxManager port with several repository calls

decisions.decision: The refresh token stays the opaque random string from login; the new Verify covers access tokens and is not on the refresh path.
decisions.why: Login already stores the SHA-256 hash; rotation looks it up by hash and checks expiry and revocation.
decisions.rejected: Make the refresh token a signed JWT

decisions.decision: Refresh gets its own httprate bucket separate from sign-in.
decisions.why: A shared limiter would let refresh attempts spend the sign-in budget.

plan.summary: Plan: one Rotate method over a transaction, revoked rows kept for reuse detection, opaque refresh tokens.
plan.key_finding: Reuse detection only works if revoked rows survive; deletion would silently disable FR-004.

tasks.summary: 16 tasks across Setup, Foundational, US1 (MVP), US2, US3, US4, Polish.

implement.summary: POST /api/identity/auth/refresh with atomic rotation, chain revocation on replay, INVALID_TOKEN mapping, and a separate rate-limit bucket.

specify.summary: Converge appended T017-T018 (jti generation moved to the use case, adapters shared) and both are built; all 18 tasks pass.

approach: Add a RefreshTokenUseCase over a Rotate port; the SQLite adapter performs lookup, expiry and reuse checks plus revoke-and-insert inside *sql.Tx; the handler reuses the existing limiter shape and error envelope.
